summary: The county page confirms $20/night, about 20 non-designated sites with electric and water hookups (amps not stated), showers, flush toilets, drinking water and dump, early May to mid October, self-register FCFS. Not waterfront stands; pin OK; phone 641-732-5204 found.
flags: PHONE missing: 641-732-5204 (Mitchell County Conservation, on Google's Otranto Park listing; the same number Google gives Cedar Bridge Park).

WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' stands, re-audited upward. The Cedar is about 70 m wide at the park, the riffle/broken dam is DOWNSTREAM below the 480th St bridge, and the park sits on the bank above it, so the below-dam rule does not apply. The gravel camping loop (~43.4591,-92.9808) is 50-60 m from the water across a mowed lawn, but a line of trees stands along the loop's river side and a 15-20 m strip of brush and weeds lines the bank (a Campertunity reviewer: weeds obstructing access to the water). The boat ramp at the SW corner is day use. The sites are non-designated, so some campers may set up on the lawn, but nothing shows the loop's sites see the river. Unsure, so no upgrade; riverview is possible for anyone on the lawn edge.
HOOKUPS: the page says 'Electrical and water hookups' but gives no amperage, so electric was not written.
PIN: stored 43.45890,-92.98107 is within about 30 m of the camping loop. OK.
